title: New MLB CBA by Dec. 1?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the MLB and MLBPA sign a a new collective bargaining agreement (CBA) by December 1, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise this market will resolve to "No".

A new CBA will be considered ‘signed’ only when the final written agreement has been formally signed by authorized representatives of both the MLB and the MLB Players Association. Tentative agreements, ratifications, or agreements pending signature do not qualify.

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices "No" at 63% for a new MLB CBA by Dec. 1, driven by the absence of formal negotiations despite the current agreement's expiration at 11:59 p.m. ET that date. Reports indicate owners and MLBPA plan to start talks soon—potentially May or June—with a salary cap as the core dispute, echoing past labor strife like the 99-day 2022 lockout. Both sides have stockpiled funds (MLBPA at $171-192 million), signaling preparations for extended bargaining over luxury tax thresholds, revenue sharing, and competitive balance. Recent April analyses of league finances underscore widening revenue gaps fueling owner pushes for cost controls, historically prolonging deals beyond deadlines.

eventMetadata.context_description: Los Angeles Dodgers hold the top spot in trader consensus at 27.5% implied probability for the 2026 World Series, supported by their elite roster depth, Shohei Ohtani's two-way dominance, and a balanced pitching rotation despite injuries to Tyler Glasnow (lower back) and Blake Snell (shoulder), maintaining a strong 22-14 NL West lead. New York Yankees trail at 13.5% with a dominant 26-12 AL East mark, fueled by surging offense and bullpen stability amid a nine-win-in-10 streak. Atlanta Braves' 10.2% reflects their MLB-best 23-11 record and recent power rankings ascent after winning nine of last 10, though recent Mariners series loss highlights rotation vulnerabilities. Chicago Cubs (5.5%) and Seattle Mariners (5.3%) gain traction from hot starts, upside pitching like Bryan Woo, and wild card positioning in a parity-driven NL Central and AL West, differentiating via momentum over pedigree.

eventMetadata.context_description: Aaron Judge commands 47.5% implied probability as the AL MVP frontrunner, fueled by his league-leading 15 home runs, 2.1 WAR, and 1.066 OPS through 37 games, powering the Yankees' AL East-leading 26-12 mark atop MLB.com's first 2026 MVP poll released May 5. A slow start has given way to a power surge, including a solo homer on May 6 versus Texas, underscoring his slash-line dominance and run production. Yordan Alvarez trails at 15.6% with a .333 average, 12 homers, 27 RBI, and 1.102 OPS for the Astros, positioning him as the prime challenger amid Houston's competitive West push. Bobby Witt Jr.'s 10.5% reflects Royals momentum and versatility, though he trails in power metrics, while Yankees teammate Ben Rice's breakout 1.8 WAR bolsters his dark-horse case at 2.5%. Trader consensus weighs early form, team standings, and historical MVP ties to contenders like Judge.

eventMetadata.context_description: Shohei Ohtani holds a commanding 59.5% implied probability for NL MVP, driven by his NL Pitcher of the Month award for March/April (0.60 ERA across five starts) and sustained mound dominance (0.97 ERA, MLB-low early), where traders prize his two-way rarity despite a .248 batting average and six homers; recent first-place votes in MLB's debut 2026 MVP poll solidified his lead two days ago, even after allowing his first homers. Corbin Carroll trails at 7% with a robust .256/.842 slash line and 19 RBIs fueling Diamondbacks' surge, while Dodgers outfielder Andy Pages' blistering .326 average and 27 RBIs (early NL RBI lead) propel his 6% share. The long season ahead, with stat fluctuations and team races key, tempers consensus as challengers like Elly De La Cruz lurk.

eventMetadata.context_description: Cam Schlittler's league-leading 1.52 ERA, 5-1 record, and 53 strikeouts over 47.1 innings have propelled the Yankees right-hander to the top of trader consensus for the 2026 AL Cy Young, with his high-velocity fastball (98+ mph) and dominant recent outings like an eight-K debut fueling the surge past injured Tigers ace Tarik Skubal. Teammate Max Fried bolsters the Yankees rotation strength at No. 2 (1.64 ERA, third in MLB fWAR), his scoreless starts through early May underscoring veteran command. Angels breakout José Soriano (1.74 ERA, 54 K) impresses with gem after gem, including a 10-K shutout, while Blue Jays' Dylan Cease leads AL in strikeouts (56) despite a 3.05 ERA, highlighting the wide-open field's reliance on sustained innings, WHIP, and matchup edges amid early-season volatility.

eventMetadata.context_description: Paul Skenes leads trader consensus at 38.5% implied probability as the defending 2025 NL Cy Young winner, building on a dominant early 2026 with a sub-3.00 ERA, elite 0.85 WHIP, and leading NL marks in ERA+, bWAR, and fWAR through eight starts, including recent gems like seven scoreless innings that solidified his top spot in MLB's latest Cy Young poll. Shohei Ohtani's 17.8% follows his stellar pitching return, earning NL Pitcher of the Month honors despite allowing his first homers this week amid a 2.54 ERA over 30 innings. Yoshinobu Yamamoto (16.5%) impresses with a 3.09 ERA and 1.01 WHIP in 43 innings for the Dodgers' rotation, while Cristopher Sanchez (9.5%) surges via a 2.39 ERA and 60 strikeouts, anchoring Philadelphia's staff. Chris Sale lags at 5.5% amid modest volume, with the field reflecting early-season volatility and health concerns.

eventMetadata.context_description: Aaron Judge and Yordan Alvarez command trader consensus at 35% and 31% implied probabilities for the 2026 AL Hank Aaron Award, reflecting their blistering early-season paces through about 30 games, with Judge leading the AL in home runs (13) and posting a 1.031 OPS on .264/.396/.635 hitting, while Alvarez counters with a .326 average, 12 homers, 27 RBIs, and 1.097 OPS. This tight race stems from both stars' elite track records—Judge's 2022 62-homer benchmark and Alvarez's consistent power production—amid a long 162-game slate where health, schedule strength, and sustained OPS will decide, keeping challengers like Cal Raleigh (9.6%, seven homers as catcher) and Gunnar Henderson viable if they extend hot starts. No major injuries or IL stints have disrupted the leaders, but rest advantages and divisional matchups loom large.

eventMetadata.context_description: As the 2026 MLB regular season hits the one-month mark with roughly 35 games played, trader consensus on win totals reflects early paces from division leaders like the New York Yankees (26-12, projecting toward 105+ wins on current form) and Tampa Bay Rays (24-12), fueled by Yankees' offensive surges including a 9-2 rout of the Texas Rangers on May 6 and consistent lineup production. Los Angeles Dodgers (22-14) top the NL West amid strong pitching rotations, while Baltimore Orioles (17-20) lag, pressuring their totals downward. Key injuries—such as Matthew Boyd's knee issue sidelining him until mid-June—disrupt rotations, with trade deadline rumors swirling around names like CJ Abrams and Joe Ryan potentially reshaping contenders. Upcoming schedule strength, bullpen health, and rest advantages will further influence implied probabilities through July.

eventMetadata.context_description: Detroit Tigers shortstop Kevin McGonigle holds a slim edge in the AL Rookie of the Year race at 38.5% implied probability, fueled by his AL-leading 1.5 fWAR, .315 batting average, and a 12-game hitting streak through roughly 30 contests, earning him AL Rookie of the Month honors for March/April and top billing in an executive poll just days ago. Chicago White Sox first baseman Munetaka Murakami trails closely at 35.5%, powered by an MLB-leading 13 home runs—including streaks of four and five straight games—despite a .239 average, highlighting his elite raw power from NPB. This tight trader consensus reflects McGonigle's well-rounded contributions versus Murakami's unsustainable homer pace, with Guardians outfielder Chase DeLauter third at 8.5 fWAR behind both, as the crowded field awaits sustained production amid a long season.

Nolan McLean's dominant pitching—2.97 ERA, 51 strikeouts over 15 starts—keeps him at 22.5%, showcasing elite stuff despite a recent bumpy outing. JJ Wetherholt's clutch multi-homer games and game-tying blasts maintain his 14.5% share, while Konnor Griffin's scorching .412/.474/.676 slash line across his last nine games has propelled the Pirates prospect to 11.5%. Trader consensus reflects this talented NL rookie class's momentum, with BBWAA voting hinging on sustained production through summer.

eventMetadata.context_description: Atlanta Braves manager Walt Weiss leads Polymarket trader consensus for NL Manager of the Year at 26.5% implied probability, fueled by his squad's MLB-best 25-10 record through early May, including a dominant Coors Field sweep of the Rockies despite Ronald Acuña Jr.'s hamstring strain. Don Kelly's 19.5% trails closely on the Pirates' surprise contention after his promotion from interim success last year, though a recent one-game suspension for an on-field incident tempers momentum. Terry Francona (11%) benefits from the Reds' buy-in to his veteran leadership amid their solid start, while Dave Roberts (8.5%) holds steady with the Dodgers' division lead. With the season young and multiple new managers like Craig Stammen and Blake Butera shining, records, turnarounds, and injury resilience will dictate shifts ahead of BBWAA balloting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Early-season small-sample volatility has produced a dead heat in the Outstanding Designated Hitter race, with trader consensus pricing Giancarlo Stanton (48.5¢), Brett Baty (48.0¢), Joc Pederson (48.0¢), and Nick Castellanos (48.0¢) as virtual co-favorites, while preseason standouts like Shohei Ohtani (47.5¢) and Kyle Schwarber (47.5¢) lurk close behind. Stanton's edge stems from his league-leading average exit velocity (94.1 mph) and steady output (.256 AVG, 3 HR, 14 RBI over 24 games), bolstered by recent multi-hit efforts amid Yankee Stadium's short porch. Baty's multi-positional versatility (including DH stints) and 12 RBIs offset a .214 AVG, while Pederson (.205, 2 HR) and Castellanos (.191, 1 HR) sustain parity through power flashes and RBI contributions in limited action, underscoring the crowded field before plate appearances solidify eligibility.

eventMetadata.context_description: Patrick Bailey leads trader consensus for the NL Platinum Glove at 56.3% implied probability, fueled by his back-to-back Rawlings Gold Glove wins at catcher in 2024-25, elite pop time, framing runs, and arm strength that ranked him MLB's top defender entering 2026 per analysts, with solid early-season stats including 228 putouts and 11 assists over 29 games. The tight clustering around 48% for challengers like Gabriel Moreno, Matt Olson (+4 Total Zone Runs, 30 double plays at first base), Ezequiel Tovar (88 assists at shortstop), Brice Turang (22 double plays at second), and leaders Matt Chapman (+9 Total Zone Runs at third) and Pete Crow-Armstrong (+9-11 DRS in center) reflects early-season volatility, where high-volume infield plays and outfield range have propelled multi-position contenders in DRS and Total Zone metrics after roughly 35 games.

The Milwaukee Brewers' pitching staff came closest yesterday, May 1, with a combined no-hitter broken up by Daylen Lile's seventh-inning double, while Guardians rookie Parker Messick carried a hitless effort into the ninth on April 16 before yielding to Leody Taveras. Historical norms average 2-3 no-hitters annually, often combined from starters and relievers, with over 1,900 contests left including potential playoff matchups. Traders monitor ongoing pitcher form, bullpen reliability, team droughts like Cleveland's 45-year gap, and park factors amid early-season pitching edges.

eventMetadata.context_description: Kyle Schwarber leads trader consensus at 49% implied probability for MLB home runs leader after blasting 11 early-season long balls, closely trailed by Elly De La Cruz at 43% with 10 homers amid a scorching Reds hot streak including multi-HR games last week. The race stays tight with a cluster of sluggers at 10-12 HR—Yordan Alvarez and Aaron Judge tied at 12, James Wood's rookie power surge at 10—reflecting volatile small-sample paces after roughly 30 games. Favorable ballparks like Citizens Bank and Great American, plus soft remaining schedules against middling rotations, sustain contention, while health, barrel rates, and platoon splits will dictate separation over 132 games left in the regular season.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Philadelphia Phillies' abrupt firing of manager Rob Thomson after a dismal 9-19 start to the 2026 season, coupled with Alex Cora's rejection of their immediate offer, has fueled a wide-open search for the permanent skipper, keeping Polymarket odds tightly clustered around 25-26% across top candidates like Brandon Hyde, Ryan Flaherty, Rocco Baldelli, and Kai Correa. Don Mattingly's promotion to interim role through season's end provides short-term stability but draws no consensus as the long-term choice, as president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski eyes proven tacticians with World Series experience or coaching pedigrees amid the club's NL East contender expectations. Absent interview leaks or favorites emerging in the 48 hours since the change, trader sentiment reflects evenly matched stylistic fits and availability from sitting managers, ex-skippers like Brad Ausmus and Mattingly, and rising bench coaches.

title: MLB: 4-homer game in 2026?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if any player hits four or more home runs in a single game during the 2026 MLB regular season. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Four home runs by a player in any length regular season game will count toward resolution. Inside-the-park home runs will count toward a “Yes” resolution for this market.

If the 2026 MLB regular season is cancelled, postponed after October 11, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, or if it cannot be determined if a player hit four home runs in a single game within that timeframe, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be official information from the MLB; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus prices "No" at 68% implied probability for any MLB player achieving a 4-homer game in 2026, driven by the feat's extreme historical rarity—only 21 instances across 150 years, with the last in 2025—coupled with no such explosion through nearly 30 games per team. Despite a power surge led by Aaron Judge and Munetaka Murakami (12 home runs apiece), Yordan Alvarez (double-digit totals), and frequent multi-homer outings like Matt Olson's recent barrage and nine two-homer games on April 14, no batter has reached three homers in a contest amid deeper bullpens, elite pitching rotations, and matchup variances. With the season young, strong closers and park factors continue suppressing historic outbursts.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Baltimore Orioles (17-20, third in AL East) visit the Miami Marlins (16-21, fourth in NL East) at loanDepot park in a potential series finale, with trader consensus reflecting a tight matchup driven by Marlins RHP Max Meyer's strong form (2-0, 2.70 ERA) against Orioles LHP Cade Povich (1-1, 5.30 ERA). Both sub-.500 teams grapple with injuries, including Marlins OF Griffin Conine (hamstring, 10-day IL) and Orioles INF Jordan Westburg (UCL tear, 60-day IL); Marlins home advantage and bullpen depth could counter Baltimore's recent bats.
